sources.title: Choose the right vehicle lighting

sources.locator: Printed pp.8–9, PDF page 5 of 7: Fog, heavy rain or snow

sources.title: Vision Impairment and DMV Requirements
sources.version: Live page; update date not displayed
sources.excerpt: central vision is used to discern detail
sources.supports: Central detail/sign reading; peripheral hazard/traffic-change detection and head/eye movement to inspect centrally.

sources.title: Halvljus – vanligaste felet vid besiktning
sources.supports: Passenger cars can have defective dipped headlights; supports the possibility of an unlit lamp on a wider vehicle.
sources.scope_limits: Single-visible-lamp width caution is an explicitly identified editorial inference from the agency fact of defective car headlights. The agency does not directly describe this night-driving illusion; no statistics or assertion that every single light is a car.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

sources.title: Winter Driving — Bridges Freeze First
sources.version: Live safety page; date not displayed
sources.locator: Bridges Freeze First, text and alt text
sources.excerpt: the cold air surrounds the bridge both above and below
sources.supports: Open air above/below bridge enables earlier freezing than nearby roads; slow before possible ice.
sources.fallback_reason: TRV På glid? (21 November 2025) confirms exposed bridges cool quickly but does not explicitly teach above/below mechanism. TS/TRV/SMHI searches did not locate that full mechanism; NWS provides exact official explanation.
sources.scope_limits: A bridge can freeze sooner, not a guarantee every bridge always freezes first; moisture, temperature and local conditions matter. No US winter casualty figures imported.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

sources.title: På glid? Nej! Så jobbar vi mot halka
sources.locator: Kan det bli halt trots att det är plusgrader? Ishalka bullet; Du kan göra mycket själv items 1 and 4
sources.excerpt: vägen ser våt ut snarare än hal
sources.supports: Water freezes on an ice-cold road into deceptive ice; air may be above zero; rain near freezing calls for speed/space adaptation.
sources.scope_limits: Road surface must be cold enough for freezing; near-zero air or rain alone does not prove ice. No salt-temperature or maintenance-performance claims imported. SMHI Trafikväder/Underkylt regn checked as corroboration only; TRV supports the teaching so no redundant SMHI citation added.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

sources.title: Arrive safely with these winter driving safety tips
sources.locator: Reduce Your Speed, bullet beginning Slow down at the first sign of rain
sources.excerpt: oil and dust have not washed away
sources.supports: First rain after dry spell can be particularly slippery because accumulated oil/dust remain.
sources.fallback_reason: Exact dry-spell/residue mechanism not located in TS/TRV inspected searches. UK Highway Code covers diesel spills/wet roads, not complete mechanism. Official county fire explanation selected.
sources.scope_limits: Hazard explanation only. No US speed reductions, car-length following rules, lighting rules or chains instructions imported. Rain and residues can reduce grip; no fixed duration or claim rain later guarantees clean/safe road.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

sources.title: Electronic Stability Control Systems — final-rule technical appendix
sources.version: Docket NHTSA–2007–27662; 2007 prepublication final-rule PDF, 327 pages
sources.locator: What NHTSA Means by Mitigating Excessive Understeer, Case 1, PDF/numbered p.310; Case 3 p.311
sources.excerpt: how sharply the vehicle can turn is limited by the friction
sources.supports: Front-axle saturation limits turn; further steering cannot tighten curve. Rear-first saturation produces rapid rear rotation.
sources.fallback_reason: VTI report gives understeer path and axle-grip framework but not the explicit front-axle limit passage in plain detail. NHTSA appendix supplies exact front-contact mechanism.
sources.scope_limits: Technical grip-limit explanation only; no US ESC compliance rules imported. Restricted to loss-of-grip understeer, not claim that every ordinarily understeering car has already lost grip.
sources.retrieval_method: Direct official primary page or PDF; exact passage inspected

sources.title: Managing Speed — Online Driver’s Manual, Chapter 3
sources.version: Live official manual; update date not displayed
sources.locator: Road Conditions — Hydroplaning, definition and response items 1–4
sources.excerpt: Do not slam on the brakes or try to turn suddenly
sources.supports: Water film disrupts tyre grip/contact; slowly release accelerator, avoid abrupt braking/steering; gradually contact returns.
sources.fallback_reason: TS/TRV results and VTI friction report cover drainage/friction risk, but no exact full definition and driver response located. UK rule 227 supplies easing/slowing only; PennDOT provides full essential advice.
sources.scope_limits: Aquaplaning response with space/time to slow gradually. No foreign mph/water-depth thresholds or emergency-law rules imported. No universal never-brake instruction. Immediate collision emergency remains context-specific; G2 ABS instruction is not a claim ABS restores water-separated contact.
